Senses.Explanation: The true eye is an eye described as correct or authoritative, especially the capacity by which an encounter or saying is distinguished without being fooled. Questions ask for the monastic’s true eye, addresses say it opens or circulates, and the thousand-hand case asks which eye is the true one; these predicates keep eye-imagery and discernment together.
